sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, and it is initialized lazily upon first access.
sketches.resonance: Declaring someone as an `object` means the language itself guarantees there will never be another — uniqueness enforced at the type level.

sketches.mechanism: Optional chaining silently collapses to nil if any link in the chain is absent — the entire expression evaluates to nothing without error.
sketches.resonance: Each `?.` is an act of reaching for something that might not be there, and when it isn't, the silence is total — no crash, no complaint, just nil.

sketches.mechanism: Method `method_missing` is invoked whenever an object receives a message it does not understand — the object can respond to anything, but knows nothing.
sketches.resonance: An object that catches every call but has no real methods is something that appears to listen to everything you say while understanding none of it.
sketches.draft:
class Stranger
  def method_missing(*)
    self
  end
end

s = Stranger.new
s.are.you.there
s.do.you.remember
s.please
